subject: Order Form — invoicing & VAT treatment / minimal commit clarification
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medisys.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medisys Procurement <procurement@medisys.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Order Form — commercial questions and VAT handling

Hi Grace,

Thanks for sending the draft order form over this morning. Procurement and I reviewed the document and we have a few commercial clarifications and a small set of redlines attached (medisys_redlines.docx). High level:

- Minimum commit: Can you confirm whether the minimum commit is enforceable per-entity or at the consolidated account level? We need it to live at the Medisys EU entity (so we can ring-fence liability).
- Net terms: Our standard is Net60 for new vendor relationships. Would Redwood consider Net60 for the first 12 months?
- Invoicing cadence & PO routing: We need invoices to be sent to finance-eu@medisys.com and a PO will be issued per quarter (attached PO template). Can you confirm Redwood will accept PO-based invoicing and map invoices to the PO numbers?
- VAT / Reverse charge: We're an EU VAT-registered entity (see attached VAT certificate). We believe reverse-charge should apply for these services — please confirm Redwood's expected tax treatment and whether you will gross-up or accept reverse-charge.

We flagged a couple of MSA clauses too (indemnity and data residency) — those are in the doc but procurement asked us to start with the Order Form commercials first. Can we get a short call this week to close pricing/po/net terms?

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Head of Procurement | Medisys Health
alex.torres@medisys.com | +44 7700 123456

Attachments: medisys_redlines.docx, Medisys_PO_4567.pdf, medisys_vat_certificate.pdf

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medisys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:28:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — commercial questions and VAT handling

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Ben (Commercials) and Kimberly/Markus from legal so we can coordinate responses and a short review of the redlines.

Quick responses before we dive into legal language:
- Minimum commit: Redwood typically ties the minimum commit to the billing entity on the Order Form. We can map the commit to your EU entity — we'll confirm the legal text with Markus but that approach is workable.
- Net terms: Our standard is Net45; moving to Net60 materially increases credit risk on small pilots. Ben, can you comment on whether we can accept Net60 for a 12-month ramp?
- PO routing & invoicing: We can send invoices to finance-eu@medisys.com and include a PO reference on each invoice. We usually invoice monthly in arrears, but we can discuss a quarterly PO mapping if Medisys requires it.
- VAT / Reverse charge: We typically issue gross invoices and accept reverse charge where applicable, provided we have a valid VAT registration number and certificate on file. Markus — please see Alex's certificate and advise on the exact wording we should include in the Order Form VAT clause.

I'll schedule a 30-minute slot for tomorrow to do a live redline walk-through; if that doesn't work, we can resolve in email. HubSpot deal is linked here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/MD-20261051.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +44 7533 987654

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medisys.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 11:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — commercial questions and VAT handling

Alex / team — quick commercial read from my side after looking at the redlines:

> On Mon, 22 Mar 2027 at 14:12, Alex Torres wrote:
> > - Minimum commit: Can you confirm whether the minimum commit is enforceable per-entity or at the consolidated account level?

We can map the minimum commit to the EU entity as Grace suggested. If procurement needs the commit to be capped at that entity, we'll add a carve-out in the Order Form specifying the bill-to entity and cap the financial remedies to that legal entity only. That should address the ring-fencing ask.

> > - Net terms: Our standard is Net60...

Net60 is tougher for us on a brand-new account when the commitment is small. Proposed compromise: Net45 standard, with an explicit 60-day payment window only if Medisys signs a 12-month minimum commit at or above the pricing band in Section 2. If commit < 12 months or below band, then Net45 applies. This balances credit exposure and your request.

> > - Invoicing cadence & PO routing...

We can accept PO-based invoices and will include PO number mapping in the invoice reference. Operational ask: finance team to confirm whether they need 'invoice per PO' or 'invoices that reference the PO' — we typically do the latter.

> > - VAT / Reverse charge...

We accept reverse-charge where legally correct. We need a copy of the VAT certificate and a signed statement confirming the EU entity is the customer of record. We'll include contract language that Redwood will not add VAT where reverse-charge applies and Medisys will self-account.

I'll be on the call to agree final pricing bands if you want. If procurement prefers, we can do the redline via tracked changes and run a short legal handoff.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medisys.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 16:22:00 +01:00
Subject: Fw: Order Form — commercial questions and VAT handling

Alex / Grace / team,

Forwarding our proposed legal language for the Order Form VAT and payment clauses. Below is the text we'd like to insert (clean copy) — Kimberly will pick up final drafting if you want tracked changes.

--- proposed insert for Order Form VAT / Invoicing ---
1) Tax treatment: Where applicable, Redwood will issue invoices exclusive of VAT and the Parties agree that the reverse-charge mechanism shall apply. Customer shall provide a valid VAT identification number and a copy of the certificate. Customer is responsible for self-accounting any VAT under the reverse charge rules of the relevant jurisdiction.
2) Billing entity and liability cap: The financial obligations under this Order Form shall be limited to the Customer entity identified as the "bill-to" party on the signature page. No other Group entity of Customer shall be liable for payment under this Order Form.
3) Payment terms: Standard payment terms are Net45. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood agrees to Net60 for an initial 12-month committed term where the Customer signs the pricing band set forth in Section 2.
4) Invoice routing: Invoices will be delivered electronically to the invoice address specified on the Order Form and shall contain any Customer PO number provided. Redwood shall not be required to produce invoices with multiple PO numbers per line item; a single reference field is acceptable.
--- end proposed insert ---

Note: we resisted language that requires Redwood to gross-up invoices for VAT where reverse-charge applies. That is commercially inconsistent with our operating model. If Medisys' local tax counsel insists on gross-up language, we'll need a commercial concession.

Please confirm if the proposed insert is acceptable and we'll bake it into OrderForm_v1.pdf and send for signature (DocuSign link will follow).

Regards,
Markus Klein
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
